allocation_frame.parent_objective: Launch a purchasable product page in the current release window.
allocation_frame.target_threshold: The page is usable and the payment path is validated for launch.
allocation_frame.risk_floor: Do not launch with an unvalidated payment path or a release-blocking page defect.
allocation_frame.evidence_ceiling: Current evidence supports release-window allocation only; it does not prove production revenue or long-term conversion impact.

candidates.action_statement: Spend the next engineer-day improving animation polish.
candidates.expected_target_effect: May improve presentation after the current page usability threshold has been reached.
candidates.deadline_or_window: Can be delayed until after launch validation.
candidates.downside: Consumes the only engineer-day before payment acceptance is complete.
candidates.reversibility: High; completed polish remains reusable if work pauses.

candidates.action_statement: Spend the next engineer-day validating the payment path.
candidates.expected_target_effect: May close the launch acceptance item that is currently incomplete.
candidates.deadline_or_window: Delay consumes the current release window.
candidates.downside: The first validation attempt may reveal a broader implementation defect.
candidates.reversibility: High for the validation action; any discovered defect creates a new decision.

candidates.action_statement: Keep the engineer-day uncommitted for a possible release incident.
candidates.expected_target_effect: May preserve response capacity if a release-blocking incident appears.
candidates.deadline_or_window: Reserve value expires at the payment validation checkpoint.
candidates.downside: Unused reserve delays payment validation without producing evidence.
candidates.reversibility: High; reserve can be released at its named trigger.

evidence.statement: The product page meets the current usability threshold.
Payment validation has not passed launch acceptance.
evidence.claim_ceiling: Supports payment-path acceptance status for this release window only.

evidence.statement: A previous release window was missed after acceptance validation started late.
evidence.claim_ceiling: Supports scoped historical delay risk only; it does not prove the current release will fail.

evidence.statement: Several engineer-days have already been spent on page work.
evidence.claim_ceiling: Supports historical spend only; historical spend is not a continuation reason.

evidence.statement: The release owner requires payment acceptance before launch.
evidence.claim_ceiling: Supports the current launch authority boundary only.

assumptions.statement: One engineer-day is enough to produce a decision-relevant payment validation result.
assumptions.overturn_condition: The first validation attempt reveals a broader implementation defect.

assumptions.statement: Another engineer-day of animation work would improve presentation but is not known to change launch acceptance.
assumptions.overturn_condition: New acceptance criteria or measured user evidence make animation a launch requirement.

assumptions.statement: A release incident is possible but not currently observed.
assumptions.overturn_condition: A confirmed incident activates response capacity or the payment checkpoint passes without an incident.

assumptions.statement: Switching from page polish to payment validation requires only a short context change within the same engineer-day.
assumptions.overturn_condition: The engineer reports a larger setup or dependency cost.

assumptions.statement: One additional engineer-day is the next meaningful polish tranche.

context_items.statement: Decide where the next engineer-day should go.
The user values release quality and does not want presentation work to delay an unresolved launch requirement.
context_items.decision_relevance: Constrains acceptable trade-offs without proving factual status.

context_items.statement: The release owner controls launch acceptance and this allocation window.
context_items.authority_scope: Current release-window allocation and launch acceptance.
context_items.authority_expiry: End of the current release window.

context_items.statement: A previous agent recommended finishing animation polish because it was nearly complete.
The designer says the animation is the most visible sign of quality.
context_items.decision_relevance: Represents advocacy but not accepted evidence.

context_items.statement: The team previously lost a release window because acceptance validation started too late.
context_items.decision_relevance: Scoped background for delay risk; it does not inherit current authority.

switching_costs.cost: A short context switch within the same engineer-day.

reusable_assets.asset: The completed page and existing animation work remain reusable after switching.

remaining_costs.cost: One engineer-day for the next polish tranche.
One engineer-day for a decision-relevant validation result.

commitments.statement: Payment acceptance is required before launch.

source_inventory.summary: Current page and payment acceptance status.
source_inventory.decision_relevance: Supports the current target threshold and unresolved acceptance item.

source_inventory.summary: Current work, switching estimate, remaining costs, and historical spend.

known_omissions: No production conversion data is available.
